battle.name: 左孝友起義
battle.brief: 大業十年（614）十二月，隋煬帝三征高句麗失敗、全境群盜並起之際，齊郡賊帥左孝友聚眾十萬屯於蹲狗山。郡丞張須陀不急於強攻，只列營逼近、斷其汲糧，孝友窘迫出降；其黨解象、王良、鄭大彪、李宛各萬計之眾隨後被逐一掃平。卡面科林斯青銅盔在東亞並無對應物，只作對照：蹲狗山真正對峙的，是隋軍兜鍪札甲與叛軍徒手標槍。

kit.name: 科林斯青銅盔
kit.history: 全正面開眼的青銅盔。看得見的代價是：戴它的人只能靠隊形活。

countries: 這場起義發生在大業十年（614）隋朝崩解的前夜，交戰雙方一邊是仍然握有正統名義的官府，一邊是因饑荒與兵役而聚集成軍的流民集團。隋方在齊郡的指揮核心是郡丞張須陀。隋代州郡各置郡丞，掌佐守與武備，張須陀以郡丞之身統齊郡兵，屯於郡治臨淄；此役既平，他以功遷齊郡通守，並領河南道十二郡的黜陟討捕大使，權柄由一郡而及於一道。黜陟討捕大使是隋唐之間常設的地方軍政差遣，既考察官吏升降，也統率郡兵討捕群盜，是中央兵制崩壞之後、朝廷把平亂任務下放給地方將領的制度雛形。叛軍方面則完全沒有建制：左孝友是齊郡本地人，糾合的是各縣逃戶、屯田逃卒與散兵游勇，號稱十萬眾，分屯於齊郡南境山區，沒有旗號、沒有部將分編，也沒有穩定的糧秣來源，幾十股人馬靠同一個首領的名望臨時聚合。戰爭的性質因此不是兩軍對陣，而是一方以郡兵與營壘封鎖山路、逼迫對方斷糧出降，另一方以占地待援、拖到官軍主力回援為目的。
countriesEn: This uprising broke out on the eve of the collapse of the Sui dynasty, in the tenth year of the Daye era (614), between one side that still held the legitimate mandate of the government and one side formed out of famine-stricken refugees and conscripts. On the government side the command core in Qi commandery was the assistant prefect Zhang Xutuo. Under the Sui, every prefecture and commandery had an assistant prefect who handled the administration and the military register, and Zhang Xutuo commanded the troops of Qi commandery from the commandery seat at Linzi. After the affair was settled he was promoted on merit to the acting prefect of Qi and was granted the title of Inspector of Promotions and Demotions and Commander for the Suppression of Bandits over the twelve commanderies of the Henan circuit: a post that in practice meant the right to inspect and rank officials and to lead the local county troops against rebels. It was the institutional embryo of the arrangement by which, once the central army had broken down, the court handed the task of putting down disorder to provincial commanders. The rebel side had no organisation at all. Zuo Xiaoyou was a native of Qi commandery; what he gathered were absentees from the counties, deserters from the state farms and scattered soldiers, who claimed one hundred thousand men and camped in the hills south of the commandery. There were no banners, no assigned commanders and no steady source of provisions: dozens of bands were held together only by the reputation of a single leader. The war was therefore not a battle between two armies but a contest in which one side sealed the mountain roads with county troops and entrenchments, trying to starve the other into surrender, while the other side held the heights and waited for the main body of the imperial army to come back.
people: 核心人物是左孝友與張須陀。左孝友，齊郡人，出身寒素，靠在鄉里的号召力起事，是隋末群盜之中少數明確以郡為根據地的首領；眾至十萬屯於蹲狗山，據高臨下，卻沒有可用的攻守器械，也沒有後方。張須陀是弘農華陰人，早年仕北周，隋文帝時已為將，積功入禁軍，大業以來轉任地方，專司討平群盜。他的辦法與左孝友正好相反：不急著攻山，而是列營逼之，斷其汲道與糧道，等山上的十萬眾自行崩潰。左孝友窘迫出降後，他以功升遷，威振東夏。張須陀麾下最出名的兩名將士，正是《資治通鑑》記在祝阿之役的羅士信與歷城秦叔寶。羅士信本齊州歷城人，年十四即為須陀所擢，驍勇而善槊；秦叔寶即後來唐初名將秦瓊，歷城人，同在須陀麾下。隋煬帝楊廣是這場衝突背後的決策者：大業十年他第三次親征高句麗，八月自懷遠鎮班師，十月至東都又還西京，十二月再如東都，同月下詔大赦天下，卻同時把董純這類平賊有功而為人譖諷的將領鎖詣東都誅殺，朝廷對地方軍力的猜忌與對亂源的處理自相矛盾，左孝友這類嘯聚山區的集團便在這樣的縫隙裡坐大。
peopleEn: The central figures are Zuo Xiaoyou and Zhang Xutuo. Zuo Xiaoyou was a native of Qi commandery of humble origin, and he rose through his standing among his own countrymen; he was one of the few rebel leaders of the late Sui who clearly organised around a commandery as a base. He drew up to one hundred thousand men and held them at Dungou Shan, commanding the heights, yet he had neither usable siege equipment nor any rear area to fall back on. Zhang Xutuo was a man of Hongnong in modern Shaanxi, a soldier of the Northern Zhou court who had already risen to command by the reign of Emperor Wen, and who by the Daye era had been shifted into local government with the sole task of putting down bandits. His method was the exact opposite of Zuo Xiaoyou's: he did not rush to storm the mountain but camped close, cut the paths to water and grain, and waited for the hundred thousand on the hill to fall apart of themselves. After Zuo Xiaoyou surrendered in extremity, Zhang was promoted for his merit and became a byword in the eastern regions. The two most famous soldiers under him are the ones the Zizhi Tongjian names in the fighting at Zhu'a: Luo Shixin and Qin Shubao of Licheng. Luo Shixin was also a native of Licheng in Qizhou, taken into service by Zhang at the age of fourteen, brave and skilled with the long spear; Qin Shubao was the man later known as Qin Qiong of the early Tang, likewise from Licheng, serving in the same ranks. The decision-maker behind the whole affair was Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang. In the tenth year of Daye he personally campaigned against Goguryeo for the third time, broke off from Huaiyuan in the eighth month, reached the eastern capital and then returned to the western capital, and in the twelfth month went again to the eastern capital and issued a general amnesty. In that same month he had Dong Chun, a general who had actually won against the rebels and was being slandered as cowardly, dragged to the eastern capital and executed. The court's suspicion of its own local armies and its handling of the sources of disorder contradicted each other, and it was precisely in such a gap that bands like Zuo Xiaoyou's grew strong in the hills.
kits: 卡面這頂科林斯青銅盔，出自公元前七世紀中葉的希臘工坊，是重裝步兵最完整的頭面防護：整片青銅鑄成，罩住顱骨、顴骨與後頸，只在鼻樑兩側留一對眼孔，護頰向下延伸。它擋得住正面的劈砍與撞擊，代價是視野只剩一線，戴它的人只能靠身旁的盾牌與隊形維持位置；公元前五世紀之後這式樣便被眼孔開闊的阿提卡式取代。距隋朝已過一千二百餘年，這頂盔不可能出現在齊郡的戰場上，它在此處標示的是「靠隊形活」的邏輯本身。蹲狗山一役真正上陣的裝備分屬兩個技術體系。隋軍方面，郡兵以步卒為主，頭戴皮冑或鐵札葉冑，身披札甲或皮甲，近身是環首刀與長槊、槍、戟，遠射用弓與蹶張弩、臂弩，騎兵配小盾與馬槊，營中備拒馬、鹿角與鐵蒺藜，攻城則備雲梯、撞車、橹車與飛雲梯，但此役根本未用到攻城器。叛軍方面近乎赤手：饑民與逃卒多無甲無盾，執削尖的竹竿、標槍、柴刀與竹叉，弓箭數量有限，靠山勢與結寨自守，營寨以木柵、濠溝與石塊堆疊而成，糧秣靠山田拾取與襲取村鎮，沒有成建制的後勤線。兩相比較，蹲狗山之役不是靠哪一件兵器定勝敗，而是靠一方有營、有甲、有韌勁，另一方只有人與山。值得注意的是，隨張須陀在齊郡一帶活動的秦瓊，此時裝備仍以尋常郡兵與縣吏的規格為準，他要到後來歸裴仁基麾下、隨李世民征伐時，才真正見到唐軍的具甲馬騎與大樣式的冷兵器，那時頭上戴的已是兜鍪加護耳，與卡面這頂希臘盔毫無血緣。
kitsEn: The Corinthian helmet on the card comes out of a Greek workshop of the mid seventh century BC and is the most complete head protection worn by hoplites: a single cast of bronze covering skull, cheekbones and nape, with a pair of eye holes on either side of the nose and cheekpieces hanging down. It stops cuts and blows from the front, and the price is a field of view reduced to a slit, so that the man wearing it can only hold his place through the shield of the man beside him and through the shape of the formation. After the fifth century BC the type was displaced by the Attic helmet with far more open eye holes. More than twelve hundred years separate it from the Sui, and it could never have appeared on a battlefield in Qi commandery; what it marks here is the logic of living by the formation. The equipment actually present at Dungou Shan belonged to two different technical systems. On the government side the county troops were mainly infantry, wearing leather or iron-lamellar caps, clad in lamellar or leather armour, armed at close quarters with ring-pommel sabres, long spears, halberds and lances, and at range with bows, strong-armed crossbows and arm bows; the cavalry carried small shields and long spears, and the camps were equipped with cheval-de-frise, caltrops and iron caltrops to block the ground, while ladders, battering rams, siege towers and movable siege towers were kept for assaults, though no assault engine was used in this action. The rebels were close to bare-handed: famine refugees and deserters for the most part had neither armour nor shield, but sharpened bamboo poles, javelins, billhooks and bamboo forks, with a limited number of bows, holding themselves by the terrain and by stockaded camps whose walls were stacked from timber palisades, ditches and loose stone, and drawing grain from what the mountain yielded and from raiding villages; they had no organised line of supply at all. The comparison decides the action: no single weapon settled the outcome at Dungou Shan. One side had a camp, armour and endurance; the other had only numbers and a mountain. It is worth noting that Qin Qiong, then serving with Zhang Xutuo around Qi commandery, was still equipped to the standard of an ordinary county soldier or county clerk. He would only see the fully armoured cavalry and the full panoply of Tang cold weapons when he later entered the command of Pei Renji and campaigned with Li Shimin, and by then the helmet on his head was a cap with cheek guards, sharing no blood relation at all with the Greek shell on the card.
tactics: 此役的戰術核心一句話可概括：列營逼之。張須陀不帶主力硬攻蹲狗山，而是把營壘扎在能控制山道與汲水的位置上，畫出一條封鎖線，斷掉山上取水與運糧的路徑，再以輕騎巡邏封住突圍的方向。叛軍屯山，一則居高可以四面窺敵，一則山上水源有限、糧秣只靠突擊取得；張須陀正是不給他突擊的機會，營壘一日近於一日，逼到左孝友窘迫出降。這與希臘重裝步兵的處境有同一個道理：戴封閉面盔的人看不見側翼，所以只能靠盾牆與隊形；蹲狗山下的郡兵同樣看不清山上的全貌與虛實，所以用營壘與封鎖線，抵銷對方居高帶來的視野優勢。破局之後，須陀把同一套辦法推得更遠：涿郡賊帥盧明月屯軍祝阿時，他以一萬人邀之，相持十餘日，糧盡而退，故意露出破綻讓明月全軍追擊，卻使羅士信與秦叔寶分率一千兵埋伏葦叢，待追兵盡入營柵再縱火焚燒三十餘座柵，營中大亂，明月僅以數百騎遁走，所俘斬無算。左孝友之後的解象、王良、鄭大彪、李宛各萬計之眾，也都被須陀各個擊破，一支一支掃平，未讓其合流。整體看，這是隋朝地方郡兵第一次以封鎖與消耗的戰法壓過人數數倍於己的流民集團，開了後來唐初郡兵討盜、地方團練逐漸坐大的先例。
tacticsEn: The tactical heart of this action can be stated in a single phrase: camp close and press. Zhang Xutuo did not lead his main body against Dungou Shan. He planted his camp where it could control the mountain tracks and the water, drew a line of containment, cut the routes by which water and grain could reach the top, and patrolled with light horse to seal the direction of any breakout. The rebels on the mountain could look out on all sides, but the water up there was limited and their grain could only be seized by sudden raids; what Zhang denied them was the chance to raid, and his camp drew nearer day by day until Zuo Xiaoyou surrendered in extremity. The logic is the same one that governed Greek hoplites: a man in a closed face helmet cannot see his flanks, so he must rely on the shield wall and on the formation. The county troops below Dungou Shan could equally not make out the full shape or the true strength of what was above them, so they substituted the camp and the line of containment for the advantage of height. After breaking the first case, Zhang carried the same method further. When the bandit chief of Zhu commandery, Lu Mingyue, camped at Zhu'a with more than one hundred thousand men, Zhang offered battle with ten thousand and stood off against him for more than ten days. His own provisions ran out and he fell back, deliberately showing a gap in order to draw the whole rebel army into the pursuit, while Luo Shixin and Qin Shubao were given a thousand men between them to lie hidden in the reeds. When the pursuers had gone in among the camp palisades, fire was set to more than thirty of the fenced compounds, the camp was thrown into confusion, and Lu Mingyue escaped with only several hundred horsemen, the number taken and killed being past counting. The bands of Xun Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Biaobiao and Li Wan, each with a following of about ten thousand, were likewise broken one by one and cleared separately, and were never allowed to join into one force. Taken as a whole, this was the first time the local county troops of the Sui beat a body of refugees several times their own number by containment and attrition, and it opened the precedent for the county troops and local militia that would grow powerful under the early Tang.
data: 可引的數字多來自《資治通鑑》卷一百八十二與《隋書·張須陀傳》。左孝友眾十萬，屯於齊郡蹲狗山；其黨解象、王良、鄭大彪、李宛各眾萬計，合計流眾逾十萬。張須陀以齊郡郡丞之兵討平，郡兵數目史無明文，但同一卷記他在祝阿以萬人邀擊盧明月部眾十餘萬，可見他麾下可用之兵在萬數上下。須陀因此役遷齊郡通守，兼領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使，權責自一郡擴至十二郡。時序亦見同卷：大業十年二月詔百僚議伐高麗，戊子復徵天下兵，百道俱進；三月帝行幸涿郡，士卒在道亡者相繼；七月車駕次懷遠鎮，高麗王元遣使乞降；八月己巳自懷遠鎮班師；十月丁卯上至東都，己丑還西京；十二月壬申如東都，戊子入東都。同月東海賊帥彭孝才為彭城留守董純討擒，純反為人譖而見誅。地理一項，蹲狗山的确切位置有兩說，或繫於齊郡治所臨淄之西南，或在益都一帶；齊郡即今山東省淄博市臨淄區，郡治臨淄，故此役戰場可定在魯中山地北緣、淄水與孝水上游之間。時距方面，蹲狗山之役距大業九年楊玄感在黎陽起兵只隔一年多，那次楊玄感聚眾十餘萬的叛亂同樣由郡兵與行台軍分段平定，兩役相隔如此之近，正說明山東一帶的叛與不叛，取決於郡兵領兵者的強弱，而非朝廷的實力。
dataEn: The figures that can be cited come mostly from volume 182 of the Zizhi Tongjian and from the biography of Zhang Xutuo in the Book of Sui. Zuo Xiaoyou had one hundred thousand men camped at Dungou Shan in Qi commandery; his partisans Xun Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Biaobiao and Li Wan had about ten thousand each, so that the crowds in arms exceeded one hundred thousand in all. Zhang Xutuo put them down with the troops of the assistant prefect of Qi; the size of the county force is not recorded, but the same volume has him engaging Lu Mingyue's hundred thousand with ten thousand at Zhu'a, which puts the force he could actually bring into the field at around ten thousand. For this he was promoted to acting prefect of Qi and granted the post of Inspector of Promotions and Demotions and Commander for the Suppression of Bandits over the twelve commanderies of Henan, extending his authority from a single commandery to twelve. The chronology is in the same volume: in the second month of the tenth year of Daye the assembly of officials was summoned to debate the campaign against Goguryeo, and on the wuwu day the order went out to call up the troops of the empire, all avenues of advance together; in the third month the emperor went to Zhuo commandery and men and horses died on the road one after another; in the seventh month the imperial carriage reached Huaiyuan, and the king of Goguryeo, Yuan, sent an envoy begging for peace; on the ji-si day of the eighth month the army broke off from Huaiyuan; in the tenth month the emperor reached the eastern capital and on the ji-chou day returned to the western capital; in the twelfth month on the ren-shen day he went again to the eastern capital, entering it on the wu-zi day. In that same month the bandit chief of the eastern sea, Peng Xiaocai, was captured by the commandant of Pengcheng, Dong Chun, who was then accused of cowardice and put to death. As for geography, the exact position of Dungou Shan is given in two ways, either to the south-west of the commandery seat of Linzi or in the Yindu area; Qi commandery corresponds to the modern Linzi district of Zibo in Shandong, so the battlefield can be placed on the northern edge of the central Shandong hills, between the upper reaches of the Zi and the Xiao rivers. As to timing, the action at Dungou Shan came barely more than a year after Yang Xuangan raised his revolt at Liyang in the ninth year of Daye; that rising, in which Yang drew more than one hundred thousand men, was likewise broken by county troops and the armies of the travelling administrations in stages. The two affairs being so close together shows that in the Shandong region whether a district rose or stayed quiet depended on the strength of the man commanding its county troops, not on the resources of the court.
cause: 起義的直接背景是隋朝在大業年間同時被四件事壓垮。第一是兵役：大業八年、九年、十年三度征高句麗，每次都是百道俱進，士卒在道亡者相繼，河北山東一帶的丁壯被抽調殆盡，留在鄉里的只剩下老弱與逃戶。第二是徭役與災荒：連年興工、轉運、造船，遇上水旱，民間無從存活，饑民成群，隨處成黨。第三是鎮壓本身在製造叛亂：大業九年詔為盜者籍沒其家，郡縣官吏在群盜所在之地各專威福、生殺任情，抄捕株連之下，反抗與求生合流。第四是前一年的示範效應：楊玄感以河北世族子弟起兵於黎陽，一度聲援遍及關東，雖迅速平定，卻讓朝野看見隋朝內部並非無隙可乘。於是在大業十年，隨著第三次東征抽走最後一批精兵，齊郡一帶的流民、逃卒與失業丁壯在左孝友號召下聚成十萬眾，屯踞山區另立寨落，與官軍對峙。左孝友既無遠方支援，也無外敵接應，起義能不能活，純粹看齊郡郡丞這一支地方武力的強弱。
causeEn: The immediate background to the rising is that the Sui dynasty was being crushed at the same moment by four separate pressures during the Daye era. First, military service: three campaigns against Goguryeo in the eighth, ninth and tenth years of Daye, each of them with all avenues of advance moving together, and soldiers dying on the road one after another until the able-bodied men of Hebei and Shandong were almost exhausted, leaving only the old, the weak and the absentees in the villages. Second, forced labour and natural disaster: works, transport and shipbuilding year upon year, combined with floods and droughts, left the countryside unable to feed itself, and hungry people gathered into bands wherever they went. Third, the repression itself manufactured revolt: in the ninth year of Daye an edict ordered that the families of bandits be confiscated, and in the districts where the bands were concentrated the local officials used the occasion to wield unchecked power and to punish and kill as they pleased, so that under search, seizure and collective punishment, resistance and the search for survival merged into one. Fourth, the demonstration of the previous year: Yang Xuangan, a scion of the great clans of Hebei, rose at Liyang and for a time drew answering calls from all over the eastern states; though he was speedily put down, it had shown the court and the country that the Sui was not without fissures. So in the tenth year of Daye, with the third eastern campaign taking away the last of the regular troops, refugees, deserters and idle labourers around Qi commandery gathered under Zuo Xiaoyou's call into a host of one hundred thousand, stockaded themselves in the hills and confronted the authorities from there. Zuo Xiaoyou had no support from afar and no foreign patron; whether his rising survived depended entirely on the strength of the one local force, the county troops of Qi commandery.
impact: 此役的直接後果是齊郡山區的流民集團被清剿，張須陀由郡丞升為通守、兼領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使，威名一時。但把時間拉長看，這一役的意義在制度層面更重：它證明中央直轄的正規軍一旦被遠征牽制，地方秩序只能靠郡兵與郡丞撐住；而打贏的郡丞隨即獲得考察官吏、調度一郡乃至十二郡的權柄，於是黜陟討捕大使這個職位在隋末唐初反覆出現，兵權隨著平亂的功勞一點一點下沉到州郡與將領手上，隋代脆弱的中央軍制因此加速解體。它同時是秦瓊與羅士信走上歷史舞臺的起點：兩人在祝阿之役以一千伏兵焚燒敵營三十餘柵，嶄露頭角，隨後羅士信戰歿於洺水，秦瓊數易其主而終於唐，這條人事線把隋末的地方武人與唐初的將門連在一起。宏觀而言，蹲狗山被平定並未改變隋朝的崩壞方向：大業十年冬至十一年，全國性的盜亂此伏彼起，河北有竇建德、淮南有杜伏威、江都一帶有朱燮管崇與劉元進，隋室在每一處都靠地方郡兵去頂，而頂得住的地方官越來越多，中央卻越來越空。隋亡之後，郡兵、縣兵與山東河北的部曲武裝成為唐初瓦解地方割據、編練府兵與鄉兵的底子，而這條路徑的起點之一，正是六一四年冬天齊郡那座山頭下的對峙。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the action was the clearance of the refugee bands from the hills of Qi commandery, and Zhang Xutuo's promotion from assistant prefect to acting prefect together with the commission over the twelve commanderies of Henan, which made his name known for a time. But measured over the longer run the significance of this engagement lies more in the institutional sphere. It demonstrated that once the regular forces under central command were tied down by an overseas campaign, the order of the provinces could be held up by nothing but county troops and county assistant prefects; and the assistant prefect who won was immediately granted the right to inspect officials and to direct the forces of one commandery or of twelve. The office of Inspector of Promotions and Demotions and Commander for the Suppression of Bandits therefore reappears repeatedly in the late Sui and early Tang, and military power sank by degrees from the centre to the prefectures and their commanders as the reward for putting down disorder, accelerating the disintegration of the Sui's fragile central military system. The engagement was at the same time the starting point for the public careers of Qin Qiong and Luo Shixin: in the fighting at Zhu'a the two of them, with a thousand men in ambush, set fire to more than thirty of the enemy compounds and made a name for themselves; Luo Shixin later died at Mingshui, and Qin Qiong changed masters several times before ending up in the Tang, so that this thread of personal history joins the local warriors of the late Sui to the military households of the early Tang. On the larger scale, the reduction of Dungou Shan did not change the direction of the Sui's collapse. From the winter of the tenth year of Daye into the eleventh, rebellions rose and fell all over the empire: Dou Jiande in Hebei, Du Fuwei in Huainan, Zhu Xie and Guan Chong with Liu Yuanjin around Jiangdu. At every one of these places the Sui relied on local county troops to hold the line, and the local officials able to hold the line grew ever more numerous while the centre grew ever more empty. After the fall of the dynasty, the county and district troops of the north and the private armed bands of Shandong and Hebei became the raw material from which the early Tang broke up the regional separatists and organised the fubing and the militia, and one of the starting points of that path is the stand-off on the hill above Qi commandery in the winter of 614.
result: 點算結果：左孝友眾十萬屯蹲狗山，經張須陀列營逼近、斷其汲糧之後，窘迫出降，所聚部眾隨之潰散；其黨解象、王良、鄭大彪、李宛各領萬計之眾，分別被須陀掃平，未能合流再起。張須陀以功遷齊郡通守，兼領河南道十二郡黜陟討捕大使，威震東夏，其麾下羅士信、秦叔寶隨之嶄露頭角。從戰役層面看，隋方以郡兵與營壘封鎖戰勝十倍於己的流民集團，是隋末少數乾淨俐落的官軍勝利；但放到大業十年的全局裡，這一場勝利更像一盞快要熄滅的燈：同年冬天，帝第三次征高句麗無功而還，各地盜亂愈演愈烈，朝廷屢下大赦而亂不止，一個郡丞的功業再大，也撐不住一個已把兵源、糧源與民力都耗盡的王朝。隋亡之後，蹲狗山這類「官軍以封鎖與消耗壓倒流民」的戰例，成為唐初地方將領處理群盜、割據勢力時反覆借鑑的樣板。
resultEn: To set out the result: Zuo Xiaoyou's hundred thousand men at Dungou Shan, once Zhang Xutuo's camp had closed in and their water and grain cut off, surrendered in extremity and the crowds he had gathered scattered; his partisans Xun Xiang, Wang Liang, Zheng Biaobiao and Li Wan, each leading about ten thousand, were swept up separately by Zhang and were never allowed to join into a renewed rising. Zhang Xutuo was promoted on merit to acting prefect of Qi and to the commission over the twelve commanderies of Henan, his name rang through the eastern regions, and his subordinates Luo Shixin and Qin Shubao made their names at the same time. At the level of the engagement, the government side won a clean victory over a body of refugees ten times its size by sealing the mountain with county troops and entrenchments, and such victories were rare in the late Sui. Placed in the larger picture of the tenth year of Daye, however, this success was more like a lamp about to go out: in the same winter the emperor returned from his third and fruitless campaign against Goguryeo, disorder grew worse in every quarter, the court proclaimed general amnesties without the disorder ceasing, and the achievement of a single assistant prefect, however great, could not hold up a dynasty that had already spent its manpower, its grain and its people's strength. After the Sui fell, cases such as Dungou Shan, where the government beat a mass of refugees by containment and attrition, became a model that local commanders under the early Tang repeatedly turned to when dealing with bandits and with separatist powers.
